The secret-hashing mechanism reuses Letflow.Identity's existing API-token precedent (:crypto.strong_rand_bytes/1 + :crypto.hash(:sha256, _), both hex-encoded, mirroring token_hash on Letflow.Identity.ApiToken) rather than inventing a new scheme -- grepped mix.lock/mix.exs and lib/letflow/ first and found no bcrypt/argon2 dependency and no other established hashing precedent. The design deliberately renames the wire concept 'secret' to a DB column named secret_hash (Sec 0.1) mirroring token_hash, and deliberately does NOT cursor-paginate list/1 (Sec 3.2) because webhooksApi.list() takes no query parameters and WebhookSubscription has no CursorPage-shaped counterpart -- both deviations from REQ-176's own DLQ precedent are explained inline in the design rather than silently diverging.
context.requirement_text: REQ-181: Webhook subscription schema and core CRUD context module (webhook_subscriptions, no route). SCHEMA: webhook_subscriptions, per-tenant schema with tenant_id retained (decision 0003 Decision B, same pattern as REQ-176's dlq_entries). Fields matching WebhookSubscription: id, target_url (string, required), secret (stored hashed -- never returned once created), description (string, optional), event_types (array of strings), status ("ACTIVE" | "PAUSED" -- exact uppercase strings; a DIFFERENT enum convention from DlqEntry's lowercase status, do not unify them), consecutive_failures (integer, default 0), last_attempt_at / last_failure_at / paused_at (nullable timestamps), created_at. CONTEXT MODULE: create/2 (target_url, optional secret, optional description, optional event_types -- if no secret is supplied, generate one; store only a hashed form; return the PLAINTEXT secret exactly once, as hmac_secret_once, never retrievable again after creation); list/1 (tenant-scoped); update/2 (Partial<{status, is_active}> body -- both are ways of expressing the same ACTIVE/PAUSED transition and must reconcile to the same stored state); delete/2 (tenant-scoped). NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no route/controller file (REQ-182); no delivery attempts, dispatch, HMAC signing, or the deliveries route (REQ-183/REQ-184).

task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req181-webhooks-core.md against REQ-181's acceptance criteria, per WF-02 Step 1b's hard-gate procedure: read the design file directly (not this handoff's summary), check every acceptance criterion below maps to a concrete design element with no 'TBD'/deferral, check function signatures are fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases), check error-handling shapes are explicit ({:ok,_}/{:error,_} tags stated, not left implicit), check cross-module dependencies are listed, and check the design contains NO implementation code (no real .ex/.exs code blocks reproducing actual function bodies -- signatures and type shapes only). FAIL immediately on any check failure, listing every failed check by acceptance-criterion id. On PASS, route to ELIXIR-DEV for Step 2a (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex, lib/letflow/webhooks/subscription.ex, and the tenant-scoped migration). On FAIL, route back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework, with the specific gaps listed.
acceptance_criteria: the webhook_subscriptions table lives inside each tenant's Postgres schema with a tenant_id column retained, matching decision 0003 Decision B's pattern -- verified by inspecting the migration design in section 1

create/2 with no secret supplied generates one, stores only a hashed form in the database, and returns the plaintext exactly once as hmac_secret_once in its return value; a subsequent list/1 or get of the same subscription never includes the plaintext secret or an hmac_secret_once key at all -- design section 3.1 (create/2 behavior) and 2.3 (struct has no such field) must make this concrete and structurally verifiable, not asserted

update/2 accepts %{status: "PAUSED"} and, separately, %{is_active: false}, and both result in a subscription that subsequently reads back as status "PAUSED" -- design section 3.3's reconciliation table must state the exact mapping for every input combination, including disagreeing/empty input, not just the two AC-named cases
list/1 is tenant-scoped, demonstrated by a subscription created under tenant A being absent from a list/1 call scoped to tenant B -- design section 3.2

delete/2 removes the subscription such that a subsequent list/1 no longer includes it, and a second delete/2 of the same id returns a not-found error rather than a duplicate success -- design section 3.4

no route or controller file is added or modified -- design section 0/4 scope boundary must state this explicitly and the design must name only lib/letflow/webhooks.ex, lib/letflow/webhooks/subscription.ex, and one migration file as its artifacts
the design contains no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex file content (this project's mechanical, no-exceptions rule) -- signatures and type shapes only, no function bodies
